alerts.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 28 at 3:48AM HST until September 28 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR SOUTH FACING SHORES OF ALL
HAWAIIAN ISLANDS...

...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR WEST FACING SHORES OF THE BIG
ISLAND...

.Rough short to medium period south-southwest swell from
Hurricane Nolo is expected to generate a quick pulse of advisory
level surf for south facing shores of all islands and west facing
shores of the Big Island today. While this is currently forecast
to gradually fade below advisory thresholds tonight, there is some
uncertainty in how quickly this will occur and it is possible
that advisory level surf may persist through Tuesday even as the
swell becomes southwesterly.

* WHAT...For south facing shores, large surf becoming 7 to 10 ft
today. For west facing shores of the Big Island, large surf
becoming 6 to 8 ft today.

* WHERE...West facing shores of the Big Island and south facing
shores of all Hawaiian Islands (excluding Southeast Big Island).

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.
alerts.instruction:
Heed all advice from ocean safety officials. When in doubt, don't
go out.

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM HST Mon Sep 28 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located less than one hundred miles west-southwest of Cabo San
Lazaro, Mexico, on Hurricane Nolo, located a few hundred miles
southwest of the main Hawaiian Islands, and on Tropical Storm
Rachel, located a few hundred miles south-southwest of Acapulco,
Mexico.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (EP91):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with an area of low pressure
located well east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands have changed
little in organization this morning. Environmental conditions are
conducive for further development, and a tropical depression is
expected to form later today or tomorrow. The system should move
generally northeastward and remain well east of the Hawaiian
Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams
NNNN
aiBriefing: Obecnie na Hawajach obowiązuje ostrzeżenie o wysokim falowaniu (High Surf Advisory), ale wygasa ono dziś o 18:00 czasu hawajskiego — czyli na długo zanim zaczniecie podróż za 3 dni, więc to konkretne zjawisko nie powinno Was dotyczyć. Poważniejszym powodem obecnego poziomu 2 (Podwyższony) jest aktywny huragan Nolo, kategorii 4, który znajduje się około 676 km od Waszej trasy — to stosunkowo blisko, choć dane nie mówią, w którą stronę się przemieszcza, więc nie wiadomo, czy dotrze bliżej wysp przed Waszym przylotem. Dodatkowo CPHC podaje 90% szans na uformowanie się nowego systemu tropikalnego w ciągu 7 dni, co oznacza, że sytuacja może się zmienić zanim wystartujecie 2 października. Warto śledzić rozwój Nolo i nowego systemu w ciągu najbliższych dni, zwłaszcza przed pierwszym etapem na Oahu. Na razie nic nie wskazuje na bezpośrednie zagrożenie dla Waszych dat, ale sytuacja jest dynamiczna i wymaga obserwacji.

aiUnnamedSystem.description: System (EP91) opisany jako obszar niskiego ciśnienia „well east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands”, z 90% szansą na uformowanie się w tropikalną depresję w ciągu 48h-7dni; prognozowany ruch na północny wschód, z dala od Hawajów.
